neighbours.label: the word just before an infinitive that describes what the thing is for or how hard it is (nowhere to go, something to think about, a tough thing to study, a difficult material to model)
fire: When the shelter closed, the families had nowhere left to sleep.
That lecture gave the students plenty to talk about afterward.
Glass is a hard substance to cut without the right tools.
Grief can be a strange thing to write about in public.
Fresh figs are the simplest fruit to prepare for guests.
After the flood, the villagers had little to eat for weeks.
Wolves are a very difficult animal to count in the wild.
Those old maps give historians something to argue about.
quiet: When the shelter closed, the families moved into a nearby hotel.
That lecture gave the students a headache for hours afterward.
Glass is a hard substance made from sand and lime.
Grief can be a strange thing, and it came in waves.
Fresh figs are the sweetest fruit in the market this month.
After the flood, the villagers rebuilt the bridge within weeks.
Wolves are a very social animal living in small packs.
Those old maps give historians a clear view of the town.

notes: Card: ' nowhere' x5, ' something' x3, ' things' x2, ' variety', ' easiest', ' material', ' thing'. Shared pattern: the token before an infinitive. Probes: 'nowhere else to go' 0.991, 'difficult material to model' 0.789, 'tough thing to study' 0.784, 'something to think about' 0.523; the same frames without it under 0.07. Note: the pole fires on the word itself, so the model has to anticipate the infinitive. New cases are in the test.
